registry_evidence.selection_rule: Keep structurally distinct KP formulations from literature; merge equivalent liftings into their representative family.

formulations.variant: binary item selection with single capacity constraint
formulations.description: Use binary x_i for whether item i is selected. Maximize sum of p_i * x_i subject to sum of w_i * x_i <= C. Each item either fully selected or not selected.

literature.citation: Martello, Toth (1990), Knapsack Problems: Algorithms and Computer Implementations

formulations.variant: DP network with item layers and capacity states
formulations.description: Build a network with nodes (i, d) for item layer i and capacity state d. Arcs represent selecting item i (d to d+w_i) or skipping item i (d to d). Binary flow f_a on arcs. Flow conservation at all nodes with source (0,0) and sink at layer n. Each item decision encoded by labeled arcs. Objective maximizes total profit from selected arcs.

literature.citation: Martin, R. K.; Rardin, R. L.; Campbell, B. A. (1990), Polyhedral Characterization of Discrete Dynamic Programming, Operations Research, 38(1), 127-138

formulations.variant: enumerate all feasible item subsets as patterns
formulations.description: Enumerate all feasible patterns Omega = {a in {0,1}^n : sum(w_i * a_i) <= C}. Each pattern is a complete item selection vector. Binary lambda_omega for selecting pattern omega. Maximize sum(C_omega * lambda_omega) where C_omega = sum(p_i * a_i^omega). Exactly one pattern selected: sum(lambda_omega) = 1. Original x_i recovered as sum(a_i^omega * lambda_omega).

literature.citation: Dantzig, G. B.; Wolfe, P. (1960), Decomposition Principle for Linear Programs, Operations Research, 8(1), 101-111

formulations.variant: quadratic unconstrained binary optimization with penalty
formulations.description: Encode the capacity constraint as a quadratic penalty. Original binary variables x_i for item selection. Integer slack variable s = E_C(b_s) encoding the capacity residual. Penalty weight M = 1 + sum(|p_i|). Objective: minimize -sum(p_i * x_i) + M * (sum(w_i * x_i) + s - C)^2. At global optimum all residuals are zero, recovering the original solution.

literature.citation: Glover, F.; Kochenberger, G.; Du, Y. (2019), Quantum Bridge Analytics I: A Tutorial on Formulating and Using QUBO Models, arXiv:1811.11538
